reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Checked all 25 lines. 'new skies' at 65:17 applies the ratified register rule; it is a register choice, not a cosmological claim, and it is flagged to the founder. The canon-cited 65:20 is rendered as the Hebrew promise. No line carries a project reading.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts were formed before opening wave-i2-editor-report.md. The report's F2 repeats the Gen 1:1 'the skies and the earth' statement, which confirms the 65:17 revise (the corpus has 'the skies and the land'). No verdict changed.

founderDecisionRecommendations.F1-bara: Ratify 'create' / 'Creator' for all 14 Isaiah sites (overlay bara-create-isaiah). Yes, the Genesis 'shape' should be reviewed at the next Genesis pass. Reasons: (1) the Qal/Niphal never takes an accusative of material and the lexica gloss it 'create' (BDB; HALOT brʾ I; Bernhardt TDOT 2; Schmidt THAT 1). (2) The central bara rationale's 'Piel "cut out, fashion"' is the separate homonym 'cut down, clear (forest)' (Josh 17:15, 18; Ezek 23:47; HALOT). Its '(Gesenius §17)' locator is wrong as a GKC reference, since GKC §17 treats Qere/Ketiv. (3) The central yatsar entry glosses yāṣar 'form, shape, fashion (as a potter)', so 'shape' for bārāʾ already collides with the potter's verb even in Genesis. (4) The canon itself uses 'créés, formés et faits' (Isa 43:7). Corpus finding: AMO-WOH-4:13 already renders bôrēʾ rûaḥ 'shapes the wind', an extension of the Genesis 'shape' outside the central appliesTo that is now inconsistent with Isaiah. Review it together with the Genesis decision. Options for the Genesis review: re-render 'create' and keep the bārāʾ/ʿāśāh/yāṣar distinction as create/make/form (the Isaiah model), or keep 'shape' but downgrade the central entry to speculative with a corrected rationale.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F2-65:17-skies: Accept 'new skies and a new earth' at 65:17. The verse is the creation-register merism, so the ratified šāmayim rule gives 'skies', and 'the heavens' stays for YHWH's dwelling (66:1). For reception continuity, keep 2 Pet 3:13 / Rev 21:1 ('a new heaven') in the 65:17 commentary and add a reciprocal cross-reference at REV-WOH-21:1. Correction to the stated rationale: the corpus renders Gen 1:1 'the skies and the land', not 'the skies and the earth'. The 65:17 line (correctly) differs from Gen 1:1 on ʾereṣ, so the commentary should not claim an English echo of Gen 1:1 for both nouns.

paragraphs.text: נִדְרַ֙שְׁתִּי֙ לְל֣וֹא שָׁאָ֔לוּ נִמְצֵ֖אתִי לְלֹ֣א בִקְשֻׁ֑נִי אָמַ֙רְתִּי֙ הִנֵּ֣נִי הִנֵּ֔נִי אֶל־גּ֖וֹי לֹֽא־קֹרָ֥א בִשְׁמִֽי׃

i18n.en: I let myself be sought by those who did not ask; I let myself be found by those who did not seek me. I said, “Here am I, here am I,” to a nation that was not called by my name.
i18n.he: נִדְרַ֙שְׁתִּי֙ לְל֣וֹא שָׁאָ֔לוּ נִמְצֵ֖אתִי לְלֹ֣א בִקְשֻׁ֑נִי אָמַ֙רְתִּי֙ הִנֵּ֣נִי הִנֵּ֔נִי אֶל־גּ֖וֹי לֹֽא־קֹרָ֥א בִשְׁמִֽי׃

notes.official: MT *lōʾ-qōrāʾ ḇiš-mî* is the Pual “that was not called by my name” (ASV). The LXX and the Vulgate read the active *qārāʾ* “that did not call on my name” (NRSV), which matches the active verbs of the first half of the verse. The line keeps MT. *hinnēnî hinnēnî* “Here am I, here am I” is rendered under the central `hineni-prophetic-response-formula` entry (ASV “Behold me”). The formula is normally a human answer to God (6:8); here YHWH speaks it, offering himself to a people who did not ask. *nidraštî* and *nimṣēʾṯî* are tolerative Niphals, “I let myself be sought … found.”

paragraphs.text: פֵּרַ֧שְׂתִּי יָדַ֛י כָּל־הַיּ֖וֹם אֶל־עַ֣ם סוֹרֵ֑ר הַהֹלְכִים֙ הַדֶּ֣רֶךְ לֹא־ט֔וֹב אַחַ֖ר מַחְשְׁבֹתֵיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: I have spread out my hands all the day to a rebellious people, who walk in a way that is not good, after their own thoughts;
i18n.he: פֵּרַ֧שְׂתִּי יָדַ֛י כָּל־הַיּ֖וֹם אֶל־עַ֣ם סוֹרֵ֑ר הַהֹלְכִים֙ הַדֶּ֣רֶךְ לֹא־ט֔וֹב אַחַ֖ר מַחְשְׁבֹתֵיהֶֽם׃

paragraphs.text: הָעָ֗ם הַמַּכְעִיסִ֥ים אוֹתִ֛י עַל־פָּנַ֖י תָּמִ֑יד זֹֽבְחִים֙ בַּגַּנּ֔וֹת וּֽמְקַטְּרִ֖ים עַל־הַלְּבֵנִֽים׃

i18n.en: a people who provoke me to my face continually, sacrificing in the gardens and burning incense upon the bricks;
i18n.he: הָעָ֗ם הַמַּכְעִיסִ֥ים אוֹתִ֛י עַל־פָּנַ֖י תָּמִ֑יד זֹֽבְחִים֙ בַּגַּנּ֔וֹת וּֽמְקַטְּרִ֖ים עַל־הַלְּבֵנִֽים׃

notes.official: *zōḇᵉḥîm bag-gannôṯ ûmᵉqaṭṭᵉrîm ʿal-hal-lᵉḇēnîm* “sacrificing in the gardens and burning incense upon the bricks” describes rites outside the sanctioned cult (cf. 1:29; 66:17). The “bricks” may be tiled altars or roof-tops (Blenkinsopp, *Isaiah 56–66*, AB 19B, 2003).

paragraphs.text: הַיֹּֽשְׁבִים֙ בַּקְּבָרִ֔ים וּבַנְּצוּרִ֖ים יָלִ֑ינוּ הָאֹֽכְלִים֙ בְּשַׂ֣ר הַחֲזִ֔יר ופרק [וּמְרַ֥ק] פִּגֻּלִ֖ים כְּלֵיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: who sit among the graves and lodge in the secret places; who eat the flesh of swine, and broth of abominable things is in their vessels;
i18n.he: הַיֹּֽשְׁבִים֙ בַּקְּבָרִ֔ים וּבַנְּצוּרִ֖ים יָלִ֑ינוּ הָאֹֽכְלִים֙ בְּשַׂ֣ר הַחֲזִ֔יר ופרק [וּמְרַ֥ק] פִּגֻּלִ֖ים כְּלֵיהֶֽם׃

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere. The consonantal ופרק *ûp̄ᵉraq* “and pieces” is read וּמְרַק *ûmᵉraq* “and broth” (ASV); the qere is read (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). *piggûlîm* is the Levitical term for sacrificial meat left past its permitted time (Lev 7:18; 19:7), here “abominable things.” Sitting “among the graves” and lodging “in the secret places” are generally taken as necromancy or incubation rites.

paragraphs.text: הָאֹֽמְרִים֙ קְרַ֣ב אֵלֶ֔יךָ אַל־תִּגַּשׁ־בִּ֖י כִּ֣י קְדַשְׁתִּ֑יךָ אֵ֚לֶּה עָשָׁ֣ן בְּאַפִּ֔י אֵ֥שׁ יֹקֶ֖דֶת כָּל־הַיּֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: who say, “Keep to yourself, do not come near me, for I am holier than you.” These are a smoke in my nostrils, a fire that burns all the day.
i18n.he: הָאֹֽמְרִים֙ קְרַ֣ב אֵלֶ֔יךָ אַל־תִּגַּשׁ־בִּ֖י כִּ֣י קְדַשְׁתִּ֑יךָ אֵ֚לֶּה עָשָׁ֣ן בְּאַפִּ֔י אֵ֥שׁ יֹקֶ֖דֶת כָּל־הַיּֽוֹם׃

notes.official: *kî qᵉḏaštîḵā* is rendered “for I am holier than you” (ASV, NRSV “too holy for you”). As pointed, the verb has a second-person object suffix, which suggests “for I would make you holy” (NJPS “For I would render you consecrated”). On that reading the speaker warns that his consecrated state would pass to anyone who touched him, a contagious holiness (cf. Ezek 44:19; Hag 2:12–13). The line keeps ASV and records NJPS’s reading here.

paragraphs.text: הִנֵּ֥ה כְתוּבָ֖ה לְפָנָ֑י לֹ֤א אֶחֱשֶׂה֙ כִּ֣י אִם־שִׁלַּ֔מְתִּי וְשִׁלַּמְתִּ֖י עַל־חֵיקָֽם׃

i18n.en: Behold, it is written before me: I will not keep silent, but I will repay; I will repay into their bosom
i18n.he: הִנֵּ֥ה כְתוּבָ֖ה לְפָנָ֑י לֹ֤א אֶחֱשֶׂה֙ כִּ֣י אִם־שִׁלַּ֔מְתִּי וְשִׁלַּמְתִּ֖י עַל־חֵיקָֽם׃

paragraphs.text: עֲ֠וֺנֹתֵיכֶם וַעֲוֺנֹ֨ת אֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֤ם יַחְדָּו֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר קִטְּרוּ֙ עַל־הֶ֣הָרִ֔ים וְעַל־הַגְּבָע֖וֹת חֵרְפ֑וּנִי וּמַדֹּתִ֧י פְעֻלָּתָ֛ם רִֽאשֹׁנָ֖ה על־[אֶל־] חֵיקָֽם׃ (ס)

i18n.en: your iniquities and the iniquities of your fathers together, says YHWH, who burned incense on the mountains and reviled me on the hills; and I will measure their former work into their bosom.
i18n.he: עֲ֠וֺנֹתֵיכֶם וַעֲוֺנֹ֨ת אֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֤ם יַחְדָּו֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר קִטְּרוּ֙ עַל־הֶ֣הָרִ֔ים וְעַל־הַגְּבָע֖וֹת חֵרְפ֑וּנִי וּמַדֹּתִ֧י פְעֻלָּתָ֛ם רִֽאשֹׁנָ֖ה על־[אֶל־] חֵיקָֽם׃ (ס)

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere. The consonantal על *ʿal* “upon” is read אֶל *ʾel* “into” (their bosom), with no change of sense. *ûmaddōṯî pᵉʿullāṯām rîšōnāh* is rendered “I will measure their former work” (NRSV “their former deeds”), taking *rîšōnāh* as an adjective that matches *hā-rîšōnôṯ* “the former things” of vv. 16–17. ASV takes it as an adverb, “I will first measure.” The change from “your iniquities” to “their bosom” is MT and is kept; the LXX levels it to the third person (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: כֹּ֣ה ׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יִמָּצֵ֤א הַתִּירוֹשׁ֙ בָּֽאֶשְׁכּ֔וֹל וְאָמַר֙ אַל־תַּשְׁחִיתֵ֔הוּ כִּ֥י בְרָכָ֖ה בּ֑וֹ כֵּ֤ן אֶֽעֱשֶׂה֙ לְמַ֣עַן עֲבָדַ֔י לְבִלְתִּ֖י הַֽשְׁחִ֥ית הַכֹּֽל׃

i18n.en: Thus says YHWH: As when new wine is found in the cluster, and one says, “Do not destroy it, for there is a blessing in it,” so I will do for the sake of my servants, so as not to destroy them all.
i18n.he: כֹּ֣ה ׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יִמָּצֵ֤א הַתִּירוֹשׁ֙ בָּֽאֶשְׁכּ֔וֹל וְאָמַר֙ אַל־תַּשְׁחִיתֵ֔הוּ כִּ֥י בְרָכָ֖ה בּ֑וֹ כֵּ֤ן אֶֽעֱשֶׂה֙ לְמַ֣עַן עֲבָדַ֔י לְבִלְתִּ֖י הַֽשְׁחִ֥ית הַכֹּֽל׃

paragraphs.text: וְהוֹצֵאתִ֤י מִֽיַּעֲקֹב֙ זֶ֔רַע וּמִיהוּדָ֖ה יוֹרֵ֣שׁ הָרָ֑י וִירֵשׁ֣וּהָ בְחִירַ֔י וַעֲבָדַ֖י יִשְׁכְּנוּ־שָֽׁמָּה׃

i18n.en: And I will bring forth seed from Jacob, and from Judah an heir of my mountains; and my chosen shall inherit it, and my servants shall dwell there.
i18n.he: וְהוֹצֵאתִ֤י מִֽיַּעֲקֹב֙ זֶ֔רַע וּמִיהוּדָ֖ה יוֹרֵ֣שׁ הָרָ֑י וִירֵשׁ֣וּהָ בְחִירַ֔י וַעֲבָדַ֖י יִשְׁכְּנוּ־שָֽׁמָּה׃

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֤ה הַשָּׁרוֹן֙ לִנְוֵה־צֹ֔אן וְעֵ֥מֶק עָכ֖וֹר לְרֵ֣בֶץ בָּקָ֑ר לְעַמִּ֖י אֲשֶׁ֥ר דְּרָשֽׁוּנִי׃

i18n.en: And Sharon shall become a pasture for flocks, and the Valley of Achor a resting place for herds, for my people who have sought me.
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֤ה הַשָּׁרוֹן֙ לִנְוֵה־צֹ֔אן וְעֵ֥מֶק עָכ֖וֹר לְרֵ֣בֶץ בָּקָ֑ר לְעַמִּ֖י אֲשֶׁ֥ר דְּרָשֽׁוּנִי׃

paragraphs.text: וְאַתֶּם֙ עֹזְבֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה הַשְּׁכֵחִ֖ים אֶת־הַ֣ר קָדְשִׁ֑י הַֽעֹרְכִ֤ים לַגַּד֙ שֻׁלְחָ֔ן וְהַֽמְמַלְאִ֖ים לַמְנִ֥י מִמְסָֽךְ׃

i18n.en: But you who forsake YHWH, who forget my holy mountain, who set a table for Fortune and fill cups of mixed wine for Destiny,
i18n.he: וְאַתֶּם֙ עֹזְבֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה הַשְּׁכֵחִ֖ים אֶת־הַ֣ר קָדְשִׁ֑י הַֽעֹרְכִ֤ים לַגַּד֙ שֻׁלְחָ֔ן וְהַֽמְמַלְאִ֖ים לַמְנִ֥י מִמְסָֽךְ׃

notes.official: *lag-gaḏ šulḥān … lam-mᵉnî mimsāḵ* “who set a table for Fortune and fill cups of mixed wine for Destiny.” Gad and Meni are the names of deities of luck and fate. Gad is a known West-Semitic fortune-god (cf. the place names Baal-gad, Migdal-gad), and Meni is attested only here. The line follows ASV, NRSV and NJPS in translating the names as capitalized “Fortune” and “Destiny,” which shows they are names while keeping their meaning. The transliterated names are given here. In v. 12, *ûmānîṯî* “I will destine you” puns on Meni, and the line’s “destine” keeps the pun.

paragraphs.text: וּמָנִ֨יתִי אֶתְכֶ֜ם לַחֶ֗רֶב וְכֻלְּכֶם֙ לַטֶּ֣בַח תִּכְרָ֔עוּ יַ֤עַן קָרָ֙אתִי֙ וְלֹ֣א עֲנִיתֶ֔ם דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי וְלֹ֣א שְׁמַעְתֶּ֑ם וַתַּעֲשׂ֤וּ הָרַע֙ בְּעֵינַ֔י וּבַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־חָפַ֖צְתִּי בְּחַרְתֶּֽם׃ (פ)

i18n.en: I will destine you to the sword, and all of you shall bow down to the slaughter; because I called and you did not answer, I spoke and you did not listen, but you did what was evil in my eyes and chose what I did not delight in.
i18n.he: וּמָנִ֨יתִי אֶתְכֶ֜ם לַחֶ֗רֶב וְכֻלְּכֶם֙ לַטֶּ֣בַח תִּכְרָ֔עוּ יַ֤עַן קָרָ֙אתִי֙ וְלֹ֣א עֲנִיתֶ֔ם דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי וְלֹ֣א שְׁמַעְתֶּ֑ם וַתַּעֲשׂ֤וּ הָרַע֙ בְּעֵינַ֔י וּבַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־חָפַ֖צְתִּי בְּחַרְתֶּֽם׃ (פ)

paragraphs.text: לָכֵ֞ן כֹּה־אָמַ֣ר ׀ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה הִנֵּ֨ה עֲבָדַ֤י ׀ יֹאכֵ֙לוּ֙ וְאַתֶּ֣ם תִּרְעָ֔בוּ הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛י יִשְׁתּ֖וּ וְאַתֶּ֣ם תִּצְמָ֑אוּ הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛י יִשְׂמָ֖חוּ וְאַתֶּ֥ם תֵּבֹֽשׁוּ׃

i18n.en: Therefore thus says the Lord YHWH: Behold, my servants shall eat, but you shall be hungry; behold, my servants shall drink, but you shall be thirsty; behold, my servants shall rejoice, but you shall be put to shame;
i18n.he: לָכֵ֞ן כֹּה־אָמַ֣ר ׀ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה הִנֵּ֨ה עֲבָדַ֤י ׀ יֹאכֵ֙לוּ֙ וְאַתֶּ֣ם תִּרְעָ֔בוּ הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛י יִשְׁתּ֖וּ וְאַתֶּ֣ם תִּצְמָ֑אוּ הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛י יִשְׂמָ֖חוּ וְאַתֶּ֥ם תֵּבֹֽשׁוּ׃

notes.official: *ʾăḏōnāy YHWH* is “the Lord YHWH” (overlay compound-name entry). *ʿăḇāḏay* “my servants,” in the plural, are the faithful within Israel, set against “you” who forsake YHWH (v. 11).

paragraphs.text: הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛י יָרֹ֖נּוּ מִטּ֣וּב לֵ֑ב וְאַתֶּ֤ם תִּצְעֲקוּ֙ מִכְּאֵ֣ב לֵ֔ב וּמִשֵּׁ֥בֶר ר֖וּחַ תְּיֵלִֽילוּ׃

i18n.en: behold, my servants shall sing for gladness of heart, but you shall cry out for pain of heart, and shall wail for brokenness of spirit.
i18n.he: הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛י יָרֹ֖נּוּ מִטּ֣וּב לֵ֑ב וְאַתֶּ֤ם תִּצְעֲקוּ֙ מִכְּאֵ֣ב לֵ֔ב וּמִשֵּׁ֥בֶר ר֖וּחַ תְּיֵלִֽילוּ׃

paragraphs.text: וְהִנַּחְתֶּ֨ם שִׁמְכֶ֤ם לִשְׁבוּעָה֙ לִבְחִירַ֔י וֶהֱמִיתְךָ֖ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה וְלַעֲבָדָ֥יו יִקְרָ֖א שֵׁ֥ם אַחֵֽר׃

i18n.en: And you shall leave your name to my chosen for a curse, and the Lord YHWH will put you to death; but his servants he will call by another name,
i18n.he: וְהִנַּחְתֶּ֨ם שִׁמְכֶ֤ם לִשְׁבוּעָה֙ לִבְחִירַ֔י וֶהֱמִיתְךָ֖ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה וְלַעֲבָדָ֥יו יִקְרָ֖א שֵׁ֥ם אַחֵֽר׃

paragraphs.text: אֲשֶׁ֨ר הַמִּתְבָּרֵ֜ךְ בָּאָ֗רֶץ יִתְבָּרֵךְ֙ בֵּאלֹהֵ֣י אָמֵ֔ן וְהַנִּשְׁבָּ֣ע בָּאָ֔רֶץ יִשָּׁבַ֖ע בֵּאלֹהֵ֣י אָמֵ֑ן כִּ֣י נִשְׁכְּח֗וּ הַצָּרוֹת֙ הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת וְכִ֥י נִסְתְּר֖וּ מֵעֵינָֽי׃

i18n.en: so that whoever blesses himself in the earth shall bless himself by the God of truth, and whoever swears in the earth shall swear by the God of truth; because the former troubles are forgotten, and because they are hidden from my eyes.
i18n.he: אֲשֶׁ֨ר הַמִּתְבָּרֵ֜ךְ בָּאָ֗רֶץ יִתְבָּרֵךְ֙ בֵּאלֹהֵ֣י אָמֵ֔ן וְהַנִּשְׁבָּ֣ע בָּאָ֔רֶץ יִשָּׁבַ֖ע בֵּאלֹהֵ֣י אָמֵ֑ן כִּ֣י נִשְׁכְּח֗וּ הַצָּרוֹת֙ הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת וְכִ֥י נִסְתְּר֖וּ מֵעֵינָֽי׃

notes.official: *bē-ʾlōhê ʾāmēn* (twice) is “by the God of truth” (ASV, NRSV). The literal phrase is “by the God of Amen” (cf. Rev 3:14 “the Amen”), and some emend to *ʾōmen* “faithfulness”; NJPS has “the true God.” *ʾĕlōhê* is a construct and is rendered under the overlay pattern. *hammiṯbārēḵ … yiṯbārēḵ* “whoever blesses himself … shall bless himself” is the Hithpael rendered under the central `nivrakhu-bekha-niphal-hithpael` entry. *bā-ʾāreṣ* is “in the earth” (ASV), or “in the land.”

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־הִנְנִ֥י בוֹרֵ֛א שָׁמַ֥יִם חֲדָשִׁ֖ים וָאָ֣רֶץ חֲדָשָׁ֑ה וְלֹ֤א תִזָּכַ֙רְנָה֙ הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת וְלֹ֥א תַעֲלֶ֖ינָה עַל־לֵֽב׃

i18n.en: For behold, I am creating new skies and a new earth; and the former things shall not be remembered, nor come to mind.
i18n.he: כִּֽי־הִנְנִ֥י בוֹרֵ֛א שָׁמַ֥יִם חֲדָשִׁ֖ים וָאָ֣רֶץ חֲדָשָׁ֑ה וְלֹ֤א תִזָּכַ֙רְנָה֙ הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת וְלֹ֥א תַעֲלֶ֖ינָה עַל־לֵֽב׃

notes.official: *kî-hinnî ḇôrēʾ šāmayim ḥăḏāšîm wā-ʾāreṣ ḥăḏāšāh* “For behold, I am creating new skies and a new earth.” Three decisions meet here. (1) *bôrēʾ* is “creating” (overlay `bara-create-isaiah`). The participle after *hinnî* marks an action about to happen, as in v. 18, where it occurs twice. (2) *šāmayim* is “skies.” The phrase is a merism for the whole created order, echoing the merism and the verb of Gen 1:1, which genesis-woh renders “the skies and the land”; the line keeps “skies” with Gen 1:1. The central rule keeps “heaven(s)” for YHWH’s own dwelling, as in 66:1 (“the heavens are my throne”), which is a different thing from the created cosmos renewed here. The phrase became fixed in later reception as “new heavens and a new earth” (2 Pet 3:13; Rev 21:1, rendered “a new heaven” in the corpus from the Greek singular). That form is recorded here, and the register choice is flagged to the founder. (3) *ʾereṣ* is “earth,” the cosmic register, where Gen 1:1 and the central default have “land.” *wᵉlōʾ ṯizzāḵarnāh hā-rîšōnôṯ* “the former things shall not be remembered” takes up the “former things” of 43:18.

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־אִם־שִׂ֤ישׂוּ וְגִ֙ילוּ֙ עֲדֵי־עַ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֲנִ֣י בוֹרֵ֑א כִּי֩ הִנְנִ֨י בוֹרֵ֧א אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֛ם גִּילָ֖ה וְעַמָּ֥הּ מָשֽׂוֹשׂ׃

i18n.en: But be glad and rejoice forever in what I am creating; for behold, I am creating Jerusalem as a rejoicing, and her people as a joy.
i18n.he: כִּֽי־אִם־שִׂ֤ישׂוּ וְגִ֙ילוּ֙ עֲדֵי־עַ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֲנִ֣י בוֹרֵ֑א כִּי֩ הִנְנִ֨י בוֹרֵ֧א אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֛ם גִּילָ֖ה וְעַמָּ֥הּ מָשֽׂוֹשׂ׃

notes.official: *ʾăšer ʾănî ḇôrēʾ … kî hinnî ḇôrēʾ ʾeṯ-yᵉrûšālaim gîlāh* “in what I am creating; for behold, I am creating Jerusalem as a rejoicing.” That the object of *bārāʾ* here is a city’s joy is a further sign that the verb names the bringing-about of something new, not the working of a material (overlay `bara-create-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: וְגַלְתִּ֥י בִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וְשַׂשְׂתִּ֣י בְעַמִּ֑י וְלֹֽא־יִשָּׁמַ֥ע בָּהּ֙ ע֔וֹד ק֥וֹל בְּכִ֖י וְק֥וֹל זְעָקָֽה׃

i18n.en: And I will rejoice in Jerusalem, and be glad in my people; and no more shall there be heard in her the sound of weeping and the sound of crying.
i18n.he: וְגַלְתִּ֥י בִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וְשַׂשְׂתִּ֣י בְעַמִּ֑י וְלֹֽא־יִשָּׁמַ֥ע בָּהּ֙ ע֔וֹד ק֥וֹל בְּכִ֖י וְק֥וֹל זְעָקָֽה׃

paragraphs.text: לֹא־יִֽהְיֶ֨ה מִשָּׁ֜ם ע֗וֹד ע֤וּל יָמִים֙ וְזָקֵ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־יְמַלֵּ֖א אֶת־יָמָ֑יו כִּ֣י הַנַּ֗עַר בֶּן־מֵאָ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ יָמ֔וּת וְהַ֣חוֹטֶ֔א בֶּן־מֵאָ֥ה שָׁנָ֖ה יְקֻלָּֽל׃

i18n.en: No more shall there be from there an infant of few days, nor an old man who does not fill out his days; for the youth shall die a hundred years old, and the sinner a hundred years old shall be accursed.
i18n.he: לֹא־יִֽהְיֶ֨ה מִשָּׁ֜ם ע֗וֹד ע֤וּל יָמִים֙ וְזָקֵ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־יְמַלֵּ֖א אֶת־יָמָ֑יו כִּ֣י הַנַּ֗עַר בֶּן־מֵאָ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ יָמ֔וּת וְהַ֣חוֹטֶ֔א בֶּן־מֵאָ֥ה שָׁנָ֖ה יְקֻלָּֽל׃

notes.official:
*lōʾ-yihyeh miš-šām ʿôḏ ʿûl yāmîm wᵉzāqēn ʾăšer lōʾ-yᵉmallēʾ ʾeṯ-yāmāyw* “No more shall there be from there an infant of few days, nor an old man who does not fill out his days.” *ʿûl yāmîm* is literally “a suckling of days.” In *wᵉha-ḥôṭeʾ ben-mēʾāh šānāh yᵉqullāl*, *ḥôṭeʾ* is “the sinner” (ASV). From the root sense “miss (the mark),” NJPS reads “he who fails to reach a hundred shall be reckoned accursed.” The line keeps ASV and records NJPS’s reading.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 5) quotes the first half of v. 20 as a forecast of the age in which medicine overcomes illness, and especially infant mortality. The line renders the promise of long life in the renewed Jerusalem as the Hebrew gives it.

paragraphs.text: וּבָנ֥וּ בָתִּ֖ים וְיָשָׁ֑בוּ וְנָטְע֣וּ כְרָמִ֔ים וְאָכְל֖וּ פִּרְיָֽם׃

i18n.en: And they shall build houses and inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
i18n.he: וּבָנ֥וּ בָתִּ֖ים וְיָשָׁ֑בוּ וְנָטְע֣וּ כְרָמִ֔ים וְאָכְל֖וּ פִּרְיָֽם׃

paragraphs.text: לֹ֤א יִבְנוּ֙ וְאַחֵ֣ר יֵשֵׁ֔ב לֹ֥א יִטְּע֖וּ וְאַחֵ֣ר יֹאכֵ֑ל כִּֽי־כִימֵ֤י הָעֵץ֙ יְמֵ֣י עַמִּ֔י וּמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵיהֶ֖ם יְבַלּ֥וּ בְחִירָֽי׃

i18n.en: They shall not build and another inhabit; they shall not plant and another eat; for like the days of a tree shall be the days of my people, and my chosen shall long enjoy the work of their hands.
i18n.he: לֹ֤א יִבְנוּ֙ וְאַחֵ֣ר יֵשֵׁ֔ב לֹ֥א יִטְּע֖וּ וְאַחֵ֣ר יֹאכֵ֑ל כִּֽי־כִימֵ֤י הָעֵץ֙ יְמֵ֣י עַמִּ֔י וּמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵיהֶ֖ם יְבַלּ֥וּ בְחִירָֽי׃

paragraphs.text: לֹ֤א יִֽיגְעוּ֙ לָרִ֔יק וְלֹ֥א יֵלְד֖וּ לַבֶּהָלָ֑ה כִּ֣י זֶ֜רַע בְּרוּכֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ הֵ֔מָּה וְצֶאֱצָאֵיהֶ֖ם אִתָּֽם׃

i18n.en: They shall not labor in vain, nor bear children for calamity; for they are the seed of the blessed of YHWH, and their offspring with them.
i18n.he: לֹ֤א יִֽיגְעוּ֙ לָרִ֔יק וְלֹ֥א יֵלְד֖וּ לַבֶּהָלָ֑ה כִּ֣י זֶ֜רַע בְּרוּכֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ הֵ֔מָּה וְצֶאֱצָאֵיהֶ֖ם אִתָּֽם׃

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֥ה טֶֽרֶם־יִקְרָ֖אוּ וַאֲנִ֣י אֶעֱנֶ֑ה ע֛וֹד הֵ֥ם מְדַבְּרִ֖ים וַאֲנִ֥י אֶשְׁמָֽע׃

i18n.en: And it shall be that before they call, I will answer; while they are still speaking, I will hear.
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֥ה טֶֽרֶם־יִקְרָ֖אוּ וַאֲנִ֣י אֶעֱנֶ֑ה ע֛וֹד הֵ֥ם מְדַבְּרִ֖ים וַאֲנִ֥י אֶשְׁמָֽע׃

paragraphs.text: זְאֵ֨ב וְטָלֶ֜ה יִרְע֣וּ כְאֶחָ֗ד וְאַרְיֵה֙ כַּבָּקָ֣ר יֹֽאכַל־תֶּ֔בֶן וְנָחָ֖שׁ עָפָ֣ר לַחְמ֑וֹ לֹֽא־יָרֵ֧עוּ וְלֹֽא־יַשְׁחִ֛יתוּ בְּכָל־הַ֥ר קָדְשִׁ֖י אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: The wolf and the lamb shall feed together, and the lion shall eat straw like the ox, and dust shall be the serpent's food. They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain, says YHWH.
i18n.he: זְאֵ֨ב וְטָלֶ֜ה יִרְע֣וּ כְאֶחָ֗ד וְאַרְיֵה֙ כַּבָּקָ֣ר יֹֽאכַל־תֶּ֔בֶן וְנָחָ֖שׁ עָפָ֣ר לַחְמ֑וֹ לֹֽא־יָרֵ֧עוּ וְלֹֽא־יַשְׁחִ֛יתוּ בְּכָל־הַ֥ר קָדְשִׁ֖י אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ (ס)

notes.official: *zᵉʾēḇ wᵉṭāleh yirʿû kᵉʾeḥāḏ* “The wolf and the lamb shall feed together” takes up 11:6–9, and *wᵉnāḥāš ʿāp̄ār laḥmô* “and dust shall be the serpent’s food” recalls the curse of Gen 3:14. The allusion is noted here. The central `nachash-arum` entry, which governs the adjective *ʿārûm* of Gen 3:1, does not apply to this verse.
